what_its_for: Pindolol is a beta-blocker used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). Lowering blood pressure helps reduce your risk of heart attack, stroke, and kidney problems. Your doctor may also use it for other heart-related conditions.
how_to_take: Take pindolol by mouth with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time(s) each day to keep a steady level in your body. Do NOT suddenly stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first — stopping abruptly can cause serious heart problems.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 5 mg taken twice a day (morning and evening). Your doctor may slowly increase your dose every 3 to 4 weeks as needed. The maximum dose is usually 60 mg per day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — your dose may be different based on your condition.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store pindolol tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the tablets away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Store in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about a medication take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid suddenly stopping this medicine without your doctor's approval. Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol, as it can lower your blood pressure too much and cause dizziness. Be careful when standing up quickly — pindolol can cause dizziness, especially when you first start taking it. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you. Tell your doctor or pharmacist before taking any new medicines, including over-the-counter cold or allergy medicines, as some can interfere with pindolol.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: very slow or irregular heartbeat, severe dizziness or fainting, sudden shortness of breath or wheezing, swelling of your hands, feet, or ankles, unusual weight gain, chest pain, signs of low blood sugar if you are diabetic (pindolol can mask these symptoms), depression or mood changes, or cold and numb hands and feet. Also contact your doctor if your blood pressure does not seem to be well controlled.
when_it_works: Pindolol begins working within 1 to 2 hours of taking a dose, but it may take 1 to 2 weeks of regular use before you notice a full improvement in your blood pressure. Keep taking it every day as prescribed, even if you feel fine — high blood pressure often has no symptoms, but still needs to be treated.
special_populations: Older adults: You may be more sensitive to dizziness and low blood pressure — rise slowly from sitting or lying positions. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as beta-blockers can affect the baby. Breastfeeding: Pindolol may pass into breast milk — consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose. Diabetes: Pindolol can hide the fast heartbeat that warns you of low blood sugar — monitor your blood sugar closely and talk to your doctor. Asthma or breathing problems: Beta-blockers like pindolol can cause serious breathing difficulties in people with asthma or COPD — tell your doctor about any breathing conditions before starting this medicine.
